title: Metric dependency matrix and trace lookup notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working note to help engineers and operators reason about metric dependencies, quick trace lookup strategies, and dashboard tile recipes for short-lived inference flows (prefix warm, kv-cache hits/misses, model fallback). The goal is a minimal, actionable matrix that pairs metrics to traces to accelerate investigation time and to inform dashboard composition.

Audience:
- Oncall engineers (primary)
- Instrumentation owners
- Product/feature owners doing rollout readiness

High-level constraints/assumptions (context):
- Multi-tenant inference: tenant-level telemetry exists but is sampled under heavy load.
- We prioritize a compact signal set for fast triage (3–7 tiles per major dashboard lane).
- Traces carry tokenized call spans, KV operations, and model selection events (model.variant tags).

Metric dependency matrix (compact):
- format: Metric -> what it implies -> primary trace anchors to follow -> quick check order

1) p50_first_token_ms (per-route) -> perceived UX latency for short responses -> trace anchors: client->edge-start, model-dequeue, first-token-emitted span -> quick checks: edge queue length, routing decision, model startup

2) kv_cache_hit_rate (tenant, route) -> warm-start effectiveness, cost and cold cache failures -> trace anchors: kv-lookup span (key, ttl), kv-warmup span -> quick checks: key-shard-mismatch logs, eviction events, stale-ttl churn

3) tokens_per_request (distribution) -> billing and batching pressure -> trace anchors: request.size, batching.aggregate span -> quick checks: unexpected prompt templates, client-side streaming cutoff, fanout

4) model_variant_fallback_rate -> reliability of primary model -> trace anchors: routing.policy, model.startup, fallback-invocation -> quick checks: capacity shortages, kernel/quantization error logs, admission_controller denies

5) backend_error_rate (5xx by category) -> systemic failures -> trace anchors: infra-proxy, model-worker, registry-store -> quick checks: OOM/GPUMem spikes, node restarts, image-pull errors

6) queue_wait_ms (per-pool) -> autoscaling and latency headroom -> trace anchors: enqueue span, worker-pickup span -> quick checks: pool size, rate limiter events, burst throttles

Trace lookup patterns (fast recipes):
- For perceived latency regressions: start from a sample user request id (if available) -> map to session_token -> open the trace waterfall and focus on spans in this order: edge-latency, routing-decision, queuing, model-dequeue, kv-lookup. Mark exact span durations and look for spikes in 'dequeue to first-token'.

- For cost anomalies (tokens up): pick representative tenant and time window -> aggregate traces to find largest requests by tokens_per_request -> inspect prompt templates in payloads for accidental debug dumps or repeated context.

- For fallback loops: filter traces where model.variant != primary and where routing.policy.reason=fallback -> check admission controller logs and capacity signals in the same trace. If fallback_rate correlates with queue_wait_ms, it's capacity-related.

Dashboard tile recipes (compact lanes):
- Lane A: UX & latency (3 tiles): p50_first_token_ms, p95_first_token_ms, tail-first-token-count (>500ms) with quick drill link to traces filtered by top callers.

- Lane B: Cache health (2 tiles): kv_cache_hit_rate (rolling 5m), kv_evictions_per_min with a note to inspect hot-key churn. Tile tooltip includes top 5 keys by eviction count.

- Lane C: Capacity & throttles (3 tiles): queue_wait_ms (avg), worker_utilization (p95), slot_admissions_denied_count. Drill link to node-level telemetry and queue traces.

- Lane D: Quality & regressions (2 tiles): model_variant_fallback_rate, human-eval-failure-rate (sampled). Attach evaluation prompt set snapshot id when a spike occurs.

Ownership & instrumentation TODOs (short):
- Add a compact tag to kv-lookup spans: "kv.intent" with values {read,prefetch,evict} (owner: Maya).
- Ensure request-level sampling keeps at least 1 trace/100 requests per tenant during normal load; bump to 1/10 for post-deploy canaries (owner: Ethan).
- Add route-level annotation to first-token-emitted span with model.hash and quantization_profile (owner: Priya).

Oncall quick checklist (for first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm whether spike is latency or error-driven: compare p50_first_token_ms vs backend_error_rate.
2) If latency, open top 5 traces by duration and inspect queue_wait_ms and kv_cache_hit_rate.
3) If errors, check fallback_rate and node restarts in infra logs.
4) Escalate to infra/SRE if node OOM or admission denials present.

Runbook snippet (example):
- Symptom: sudden drop in kv_cache_hit_rate for route R in last 5m
  - Step 1: Query eviction logs for shards serving R (time window -10m -> now)
  - Step 2: Check node restart timeline; if restarts coincide, correlate to node-pooling changes or deploys
  - Step 3: If no restarts, inspect recent model rollouts that increased embedding/tokens_per_request (could increase memory pressure on KV layer)
  - Step 4: Temporary mitigation: increase kv-prefetch workers for route R for 10m (ops-only), open incident if sustained

Open questions / unresolved decisions (capture here so this note is a live artifact):
- Sampling policy: do we prefer 1/100 global with 1/10 canaries, or route-weighted sampling to protect low-traffic customers? pros/cons listed inline.
- Should kv-eviction top-keys be computed at ingestion (index) to keep dashboard query costs lower?

Links/refs: Slack: #obs-instrumentation, PR: telemetry/pull/341, Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-527 (signal catalog draft).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this intentionally small. If more than three drill paths per lane, we're over-instrumenting.
- Next step: prototype a microdash with the above lanes and run a 48-hour ops drill to validate triage time improvements.
